A mask paints a box and moves nothing, so a mask on a box that can resize buys nothing"); const surfaces = fs.readFileSync("test/e2e/surfaces.ts", "utf8"); const firstScreenOnly = /VIEWPORT_ONLY_OPERATOR_PATHS[^=]*=[^\]]*\/admin\/qr/.test(surfaces); if (firstScreenOnly) { const VIEWPORT = { "admin-qr--dawn-light-desktop.png": 800, "admin-qr--dawn-light-mobile.png": 844, "admin-qr--dawn-dark-desktop.png": 800, "admin-qr--dawn-dark-mobile.png": 844 }; for (const file of Object.keys(VIEWPORT)) { const png = fs.readFileSync(DIR + file); const tall = png.readUInt32BE(20); if (tall !== VIEWPORT[file]) fail(file + " is " + tall + " px tall, but /admin/qr is captured first-screen-only, so its baseline must be exactly one viewport (" + VIEWPORT[file] + " px). A taller baseline means the surface went back to a full-page capture and the sliding 30-day scans chart is in the committed picture again, where nothing is painting over it.") } console.log("LIVE-458 ok: /admin/qr photographs its first screen, so the sliding scans window is not in the committed baselines at all"); process.exit(0) } import("./scripts/visual-diff-bands.mjs").then((m) => { const chart = (file) => { const img = m.decodePng(fs.readFileSync(DIR + file)); const isMask = (x, y) => { const i = (y * img.width + x) * 4; return img.data[i] === 255 && img.data[i + 1] === 0 && img.data[i + 2] === 255 }; const mid = Math.floor(img.width / 2); let tallest = 0; let top = 0; let run = 0; for (let y = 0; y < img.height; y += 1) { if (isMask(mid, y)) { run += 1; if (run > tallest) { tallest = run; top = y - run + 1 } } else run = 0 } let wide = 0; if (tallest > 0) { const row = top + Math.floor(tallest / 2); for (let x = 0; x < img.width; x += 1) if (isMask(x, row)) wide += 1 } return { tallest, wide } }; for (const file of ["admin-qr--dawn-light-desktop.png"]) { const r = chart(file); if (r.tallest < 112 || r.wide < 300) fail(file + " no longer paints over the 30-day scans chart: the tallest solid mask band down its centre is " + r.tallest + " px by " + r.wide + " px, and the h-28 chart box is 112 px tall. The committed baseline is photographing a window that steps one column left at every UTC midnight, which fails on whichever pull request happens to run next") } console.log("LIVE-458 ok: the sliding scans window is painted over in the committed /admin/qr baselines"); process.exit(0) }).catch((e) => { console.error(String(e)); process.exit(1) })'
verify.note: Measures the consequence, which is that the sliding 30-day window cannot move the committed picture, and it is now true by EITHER of two mechanisms, so the probe reads which one is in force rather than assuming. Arm 1 is unconditional: the mask stays registered on the FIXED h-28 box, because a mask on a box that can resize buys nothing, and because the mask has to still be there for the day the surface returns to full-page. Arm 2 branches on the capture mode declared in test/e2e/surfaces.ts. FULL-PAGE: the tallest solid run of mask colour down the centre of both committed baselines must be at least 112 px (the h-28 chart box) and at least 300 px wide, so the window is painted over in the picture the next comparison is judged against. FIRST-SCREEN-ONLY (LIVE-475, owner ruling 2026-09-23): the chart sits about 13,200 px down a 14,500 px page, so a one-viewport capture cannot contain it, and the arm asserts all four baselines are EXACTLY one viewport tall. That is a real measurement, not a skip: it fails the moment anyone recaptures this surface full-page without restoring the mask, which is precisely the regression arm 2 exists to catch. Mutation-tested four ways: removing the attribute fails it, moving the attribute off h-28 fails it, a full-page baseline with no chart fails it at 0 px, and a full-page-tall baseline while the registry says first-screen-only fails it on the height. Pure node, about 590 ms.
